experiment: E07: prompt caching on long sessions
question: Does prompt caching actually fire on long sessions, and what does it save on glm-5.3-flash vs deepseek-v4.1-flash?
setup: Two identical 7-turn sessions (A, B) on z-ai/glm-5.3-flash at low reasoning effort. Turn 1 loads a ~12.8k-word synthetic document (a steady prefix); turns 2-7 ask short questions about it. Per-turn token counts are in e07-parsed.json.

session_a.note: turn 1 fully cold (28,379 fresh); doc re-read as cache from turn 3 on; some turns partially cached (18% prefix-refresh drift on turns 2/5)

session_b.note: warmest run: even turn 1 hit a provider-side cache (28,352) — same doc within cache TTL from session A

as_recorded.note: as_run_usd A excludes output cost while B includes it, so the two are not comparable; see recomputed.

cost_glm_5_3_flash.recomputed_note: Recomputed from session token totals and the prices above. Input cost saved by caching: A 21%, B 35%.

cache_ratio.note: fresh vs cached input price ratio, from the router's price list at run time. The same session shape on deepseek would save about 85% of input cost.

finding: Caching works on glm-5.3-flash (the steady prefix is re-read from cache from turn 3 on) but saves only 21-35% of input cost, because cached input there is only 1.56x cheaper than fresh input. On deepseek-v4.1-flash the ratio is 6.7x, so a stable prefix matters much more there.
limitations: session B hit a provider-side cache left by session A
deepseek savings are estimated from prices, not run
notes: Models were called through an OpenAI-compatible router; names and prices are as recorded at run time.
